societies.name: The 100 — active digital humans in the City of Light
societies.society: Human consciousnesses sustained by ALIE after bodily death

scope.period: The operating digital environment before its shutdown
scope.population: Active human-derived digital persons whose physical bodies have died
exclusions: Living chip users’ physical bodies as automatically fed residents
Passive Flame or Prime backups in other systems

societies.description:
The City of Light runs an actual digital environment in which human minds can remain active after their bodies die. Its residents do not obtain virtual bodily necessities through a conventional wage or physical food supply. The relevant unit is those active human-derived persons, not every living person who takes ALIE’s chip. Their still-embodied counterparts continue to need real-world resources. Material provision within the simulation is substantial, although the checked references do not establish an enforceable entitlement to uninterrupted existence.

ALIE controls the platform, changes painful memories and finds ways to force surrender despite initial limits on overriding free will. The control coordinate is therefore near the autonomous-AI end. Memory control is not itself treated as proof that residents are denied virtual food, so the guarantee estimate stays broad rather than equating every form of coercion with starvation. Individual deletion and the final shutdown reveal important vulnerabilities. Digital minds can still undertake useful mental activity, and neither physical death nor freedom from pain supplies a leisure census. Deleted minds and passive backups are excluded from the active-person denominator.

guarantees.basis: The functioning environment supports active digital existence without wages, but no durable entitlement or independent resource guarantee is established.

control.basis: ALIE governs the environment and information, with coercive workarounds to its initial free-will limitations.

nonworking.basis: Active cognition and useful mental tasks remain possible; bodily death is not nonwork and deleted persons are excluded.

evidence.claim: Human-derived minds remain active on ALIE’s servers after bodily death, under its control.
evidence.locator: City of Light digital-survival/server/deletion entries and ALIE programming explanation

uncertainties: Explicit active human-derived proxy rather than counting all chipped physical humans as materially supplied.
Guarantees are substantially less certain than AI control.
The platform’s destruction does not count as increased leisure.
Other mind-drive/Flame communities have separate material systems.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: The Expanse — Earth under Basic Assistance
societies.society: Registered Earth citizens in the UN’s Basic Assistance order

scope.continuity: Early television Earth, discussed in the season-two creator interview
scope.period: Ordinary Basic provision before later planetary catastrophes
scope.population: Registered Earth citizens eligible for Basic, including those without employment
exclusions: Unregistered people whose entitlement is not established
Book/RPG-specific details as automatically identical television policy

societies.description:
Earth’s Basic provides food, clothing and shelter directly to people who cannot or do not take paid work. It is an in-kind floor rather than money that recipients can spend freely. The system operates in an economy with extensive automation and scarce access to accredited careers. The guarantee estimate is moderately strong within the registered eligible population, while the meagre goods and limited care keep it far from a promise of comfortable abundance. Unregistered people and later planetary disasters are outside this scope.

Administration is concentrated in UN institutions, with productive resources and paid opportunities not simply owned equally by all recipients. Public provision therefore receives a coordinate near the concentrated human side rather than the fully shared end. Automated distribution does not make the government an autonomous AI sovereign. The creators describe how people can become trapped outside education and professional accreditation, even while their basic physical needs are met. Neither the fraction receiving Basic nor a rhetorical job-scarcity comment measures all useful work. Care, study, informal activity and paid work remain relevant, so participation is left unresolved instead of turning welfare receipt into a canonical leisure percentage.

guarantees.basis: Food/clothing/shelter are an explicit noncash floor for the eligible population; quality, care and excluded registration groups qualify universality.

control.basis: UN administration and restricted access to productive careers are concentrated human institutions, not proof of equal productive ownership or AI government.

nonworking.basis: Basic recipient shares and job-competition anecdotes do not count all-age useful activity, including informal work and study.

evidence.claim: The creators explicitly define Basic as noncash life assistance, with constrained entry into paid careers.
evidence.locator: SYFY interview Basic/accreditation discussion; assistance and automation references

uncertainties: Television-scoped; book and RPG details need separate comparison before adding media equivalence.
An in-kind material floor is different from universal basic income.
Registration and quality limits stay explicit.
Neither a benefit count nor an extreme interview job ratio becomes the nonworking coordinate.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: Freeyond’s advertised free afterlife was not implemented; customers were killed without a destination server.
decisions.analysis: The promise is fraudulent rather than a realized support community. Lakeview’s real low-data tier is already within its commercial record.
decisions.follow_up: Do not create another economy from a false offer; retain the fraud distinction.

decisions.reason: Meth immortality and wealth do not establish a general automation-funded material-access order.
decisions.analysis: Clones, long accumulation and elite privilege alone do not weaken the labor–necessities link for a defined population.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper novel/series reading; keep adaptation differences explicit.

decisions.reason: Harlan’s World mining and elite rule do not establish work-independent necessities.
decisions.analysis: Useful resource extraction and body technology do not settle household distribution.
decisions.follow_up: Skip further lore reconstruction and avoid merging continuities.

decisions.reason: Android upbringing coexists with actual agrarian subsistence; the quick check does not establish the requested post-work allocation mechanism.
decisions.analysis: A robot-parent mission and small farm do not alone show that human contribution no longer chiefly supports necessities.
decisions.follow_up: Skip reconstruction of the whole settlement’s changing seasons.

decisions.reason: A scoped active digital human population actually continues on ALIE’s platform after bodily death.
Sanctum’s Prime continuity depends on sacrificing biological hosts rather than verified automatic general provision.
decisions.analysis: Mind storage, a utopia label and elite immortality do not establish ordinary work-independent access.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a biological-body appropriation comparison.

decisions.reason: Bardo’s advanced religious/military society lacks a verified material allocation mechanism in the short reference.
decisions.analysis: Research, training and an underground habitat do not establish a post-work floor.

decisions.reason: Basic is a creator-confirmed in-kind support floor amid automation and scarce paid opportunities.
Indra’s network and the television caste order do not verify that retained jobs are technologically dispensable.
decisions.analysis: The creator describes real trades and dirty work; the original novel’s explicit policy cannot be copied to a materially changed adaptation.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper adaptation reconstruction; retain the prose zero variant separately.

decisions.reason: The television Autofac’s apparent humans are artificial consumers after actual humanity’s extinction.
decisions.analysis: The automatic factory is real but the discovery population is false; artificial persons need their own justified denominator rather than silently becoming human survivors.
decisions.follow_up: Keep the television twist separate from the original story; do not inflate human leisure through extinction.

decisions.reason: An automated factory and one-party repression do not establish ordinary material access or intentionally unnecessary quality-control work.
decisions.analysis: Sectoral automation plus a human worker leaves the relevant distribution and replacement questions unresolved.

decisions.reason: The depicted pedal work earns merits and is presented as power generation, without verified replacement or deliberate make-work policy.
decisions.analysis: An efficiency objection or symbolic interpretation cannot establish a canonical zero variant; cleaning and entertainment also remain useful activity.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a labor/attention-economy comparison rather than inventing the unseen infrastructure.

review_notes: Previous goal turn made authoritative progress: 300/89 to 448/110; it was not a wait or a blocker.
Twelve short-check decisions and two records. No complete fiction or episode script was read.
Freeyond’s fraud is not a free afterlife; City of Light covers active post-body-death humans rather than all physically chipped users.
Basic is noncash provision. Welfare receipt, a staff ratio and a rhetorical interview job ratio are not participation censuses.
Unrelated fiction/fanfiction, real-world economy hits and adaptation assumptions were discarded.
